## Stage A Trigger
Phase 3.2 — Daily Standup Sync. Runs on Schedule Trigger at 09:00 and 17:00 Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh.

Stage B — Calendar lookup → match events by `daily_meeting_title_pattern` (system_config) → pick latest attached transcript per event (`transcript_title_pattern` + Drive modifiedTime) → fetch + clean text.

## Stage C LLM
Builds the active project index, then classifies mentioned projects and extracts concrete WIP task actions in one model call.

## Stage D Persist
Applies WIP actions with continueOnFail enabled. Create actions pass through the WIP Match Layer A guard before insert. Meeting upsert uses a get/update/create pattern because Supabase create has no on-conflict.

## Sheet Sync
wip_tasks Sheet tab mirrors Supabase wip_tasks for AppSheet. Updated on create, update, and complete — same pattern as Phase 1 Helpdesk.

## Stage E Cascade
Completed WIP tasks are looped into ticket updates. This avoids relying on a Supabase `in` filter shape that varies by node version.

## Stage F Email
Always sends a terminal summary, including zero-action runs and the double-run warning. Workflow-level Error Workflow should be configured separately for uncaught failures.

nodes.name: Gmail Send No transcript on meeting

messageValues.message: You are a meeting analyst. You receive a Daily WIP standup transcript and an array of active projects with their open WIP tasks. Identify which projects from the list were discussed. For each discussed project, output the WIP actions the team agreed on: update existing tasks, create new tasks, or mark tasks complete. Use only project_client values that appear verbatim in the supplied list. For update/complete actions, set existing_task_id to a UUID from the supplied tasks list. Quote a note tag like [29 May] in latest_note when one is provided. Output strictly the JSON object defined by the response schema — no prose, no markdown.

parameters.subject: ={{ '[Daily WIP Sync] ' + $('Resolve Date').first().json.targetDate + ' — ' + ($json.title || 'Meeting') + ' — No actionable items' }}

messageValues.message: You match candidate WIP tasks against an existing open list using semantic similarity. Be conservative: only call it a match when the proposed task clearly refers to the same piece of work as one of the existing tasks (same intent, same artifact, not just same project). Otherwise return decision=new with match_id=null. Confidence must be a float in [0,1]. Output only the JSON object required by the schema.
